subject: Private VPC: ops fallback, control/data placement and observability handoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@terracloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: ops fallback, control/data placement and observability handoff

Rajiv —

Thanks again for walking through the on-prem topology last week. Per our call, I put together a concise list of the two items we want to validate in the next technical review: control plane placement and the fallback/observability story for tenant traffic if the primary dataplane path is interrupted.

High-level asks for the review (30–45 min):
- Confirm control plane placement options (colocated in customer PoP vs isolated control cluster in the colo) and implications for latency/SLA.
- Walk through the data-plane egress/fallback behavior: NAT vs proxy, expected source IPs, and how we preserve tenant isolation during failover.
- Review telemetry handoff: what observability signals you can expose (flow logs, span bridging, KV cache hit metrics) and what evidence we need for compliance.
- Quick review of the runbook draft and observable alerts we want to create for canaries.

I attached an updated architecture_diagram_v2.png and a draft ops_fallback_runbook_draft.pdf — both are intentionally compact. Please confirm if Thursday 8/2 09:30 PT (we can also do 11:00) works for your infra & networking leads.

If there are constraints around IP allowlists or egress proxies we should know ahead of time, flag them in a reply so we can add them to the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@terracloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: ops fallback, control/data placement and observability handoff

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear list. Thursday 9/2 at 09:30 PT works for our team (I'll bring our network lead and security engineer). A couple quick notes before the call:

- We prefer an isolated control cluster in the colo (separate VLAN + dedicated management plane) for security/compliance reasons; will want documentation that no tenant traffic leaks into control.
- Egress sits behind our perimeter proxy (forward proxy) today — we will need to map how Redwood's control callbacks and KV cache prefetching traverse that path.
- For observability, we can share sampled flow logs and NetFlow-like exports; for deeper traces we'll need an agreed redaction policy because some flows include internal hostnames.

I'll upload a quick topology sketch from our side and bring the team. See you Thursday.

—Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
Head of Infrastructure
TerraCloud

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@terracloud.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: ops fallback, control/data placement and observability handoff

Rajiv / Jonas —

Adding a couple practical items from ops we should confirm during the call so we can finalize the runbook:

- TLS termination points and cert rotation: where do we terminate mTLS? If in customer PoP, we need a cert ingress plan and a rotation window.
- IP ranges and NAT behavior: list of IP blocks we will use for callbacks so TerraCloud can pre-authorize.
- KV cache warm-up: acceptable prefetch size and whether prefetch traffic should be routed via proxy or direct under a dedicated route.
- Canary & alert thresholds: proposed token drop and latency SLOs that should trigger a failover.

I've flagged the draft runbook with inline comments (ops_fallback_runbook_draft.pdf) — nothing final, but it should speed the call.

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@terracloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: ops fallback, control/data placement and observability handoff

Thanks everyone — good sync today. A quick recap of decisions and open items:

Decisions:
- Control plane will be a dedicated management cluster in TerraCloud's colo (isolated VLAN). Redwood control callbacks will use a dedicated management subnet.
- Dataplane primary path goes through our perimeter proxy; fallback will re-route to a secondary NAT path that preserves tenant source mapping.
- We can provide sampled flow logs + NetFlow exports; detailed traces will require hostname redaction and an NDA addendum.

Open items (TerraCloud action items):
1) Share CIDR ranges for the management subnet + proxy egress IPs by 9/6.
2) Confirm certificate rotation windows and whether Redwood may push rotation updates via the management plane.
3) Upload the internal topology sketch (we'll attach to HubSpot TC-3241).

Attachments: terracloud_topology_sketch.pdf (uploaded to the Drive link)

We'll circulate the agreed runbook after you include the CIDRs.

—Rajiv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@terracloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: ops fallback, control/data placement and observability handoff

Thanks Rajiv — this looks good. Action items from Redwood:
- We'll add explicit steps to the runbook for failover validation and tenant isolation verification (Marissa will own the test plan).
- I'll update the architecture_diagram_v2.png to annotate the management-subnet egress and the fallback NAT path, then re-upload.
- Kimberly will draft the alert thresholds and canary probes (we'll propose initial SLOs in the next 48 hours).

Next milestone: we'll send a runbook+diagram update by EOD Mon 9/6. If you can share the CIDRs and cert rotation windows before then it will let us finalize the evidence checklist for your compliance team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to getting this into your staging run.

—Jonas
